meta.parties: Hall v. Pelmadulla Valley Tea and Rubber Company, Limited

rules.statement: A transaction that appears to be a sale for money but is actually a transfer of land in consideration of moneys paid all intuitu, i.e., by way of loan from the purchaser to the vendor, can be considered fraudulent or collusive and thus void under section 17 of the Land Registration Ordinance of 1891.
rules.supporting_quote: The transaction, so far as the Rs. 30,624 was concerned, was not a sale for money thus paid as consideration for the transfer, but a transfer of land in consideration of moneys paid alio intuitu, viz., by way of loan by the purchaser to the vendor to be accepted, presumably, in satisfaction of the debt.
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 17 of the Land Registration Ordinance of 1891 (No. 14 of 1891)
